paper.title: On the Computational Tractability of Robust Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Linear robust bandits (Euclidean-ball arms and outcomes, affine credal constraints with transversality cutoff S)
unmapped: Robust (imprecise) bandits: a hidden hypothesis h* maps each arm to a credal set of outcome distributions (those whose mean lies in {y in D: C y + B x + d = 0}); an adaptive adversary picks any distribution in h*(x_t) each round
Regret is measured against T*V*, the max over arms of the worst-case expected reward under the true hypothesis (maximin value), not against realized rewards
Learner observes a vector outcome y_t in a Euclidean ball D (reward r(x,y)=a^T x + b^T y is a known function of it), richer than pure bandit feedback
Transversality condition with cutoff S in (0,1] on hypotheses
Arm set X and outcome set D are Euclidean balls in R^{d_X}, R^{d_D}; reward range C_r
settings.definition_quote:
An instance of the robust bandits problem is a tuple $\mathcal{M} = \left( X , D , H , r \right)$, where $X$ is a set of arms, $D$ is a set of possible outcomes, $H$ is a set of mappings of type $X \to \credal D$, and $r : X \times D \to \mathbb{R}$ is a reward function.

The robust bandits game is played between a learner and an adversary for $T$ rounds (both adversary and learner know $T$). At the beginning of the game, the adversary picks some $h^{\star} \in H$. The learner knows $X , D , H , r$, and $T$, but does not have knowledge of $h^{\star}$. Then, at each round $t$:

source.label: thm:soft-square-root-regret
source.quote: Algorithm~\ref{alg:soft-square-root} satisfies, with probability at least $1-\delta$, $TV^\star-\sum_{t=1}^Tr(x_t,y_t)\le4\lambda\left(J_{\max}'+1\right)+\frac{G^2{B_T'}^2T}{4\lambda}$.

results.notes: Realized regret against T V* holds w.p. 1-delta. Stated for exact maximization; approximate polytime implementation adds T*kappa = 1.

symbols.b_norm: ||b||_2 after rescaling D to the unit ball

conditions: true hypothesis satisfies transversality with cutoff S

source.label: thm:soft-square-root-regret
source.quote: Its expected regret is at most the same expression plus $C_rT\delta$, and taking $\delta=(T+1)^{-2}$ gives $R_T\le\tilde O\left(\left[q+\left(1+S^{-1}\right)^2\|b\|_2^2\,q\,d_D\right]\sqrt T\right)+O\left(\frac{C_r}{T}\right).$

results.notes: Regret R_T = T V* - E[sum r], where V* is the maximin value. Learner doesn't need S. Informal Theorem 11 restates this. Polytime implementation via Bienstock's QCQP solver (Appendix B.1) preserves rate.

conditions: hidden factor polynomial in dimensions, 1/S and C_r

source.label: thm:efficient-upper-bound
source.quote: There exists a policy for linear robust bandits as defined above that, for every time horizon $T$ and every true hypothesis $h^{\star} \in H$, runs in time polynomial in $| \phi |$ and $T$ and achieves regret $R_{T} \le \tilde{O} ( \sqrt{T} )$.

results.notes: Main theorem; emphasises polynomial running time in |phi| and T. Precise dependence in Theorem 21.

symbols.B_T: sqrt(1 + J_max*h_T^2), h_T^2 = 8 d_D log(2 d_D T^2/delta)

source.label: thm:hard-ellipsoid-regret
source.quote: Algorithm~\ref{alg:hard-ellipsoid-warmup} satisfies, with probability at least $1 - \delta$, $T V^{\star} - \sum_{t = 1}^{T} r ( x_{t} , y_{t} ) \le C_{r} n ( J_{\max} + 1 ) + \frac{G B_{T} T}{\sqrt{n}}$.

results.notes: Assumes exact arm choice; approximate polytime version doubles middle term and adds 1.

source.label: thm:hard-ellipsoid-regret
source.quote: Its expected regret is at most the same expression plus $C_{r} T \delta$. Taking $n = \lceil T^{2/3} \rceil$ and $\delta = (T + 1)^{-2}$ give $R_{T} \le \tilde{O} ( T^{2/3} )$ for fixed problem parameters.

conditions: via reduction from stochastic linear bandits on unit ball with rewards in [-1,1] (S = 1)

source.label: thm:lower-bound-informal
source.quote: Every learner for linear robust bandits has worst-case regret $\Omega ( \sqrt{T} )$.

results.notes: Informal; proof transfers Dani et al. (2008) lower bound via Remark 2.
